_doc: Re-authentication of the administrator settings routes (web only in v0.4.0). PATCH /api/admin/settings/auth takes currentPassword (and code from an administrator with an authenticator) when the change lowers a protection or signs everyone else out; the exact rule with its cases is admin-reauth.json. PUT /api/admin/settings/smtp (the whole settings object plus currentPassword and code) and DELETE /api/admin/settings/smtp {currentPassword, code?} always re-authenticate; PUT validates the settings first (a 422 of the mail settings spends no attempt). Note that 422 password_required on PUT smtp has two meanings: the mail account's user name needs a password (message 'A user name needs a password.'), or the administrator's own currentPassword is missing; a client that always sends currentPassword only sees the first. A new publicUrl, like a new host, port, security or user name, needs the stored mail password again (422 password_reentry_required): reset links carry it. Refusals: 422 password_required, 403 wrong_password, 403 code_invalid (see errors.json).
